sheet-55.description: Sheet 55, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the southwestern residential tract of Fort Lee next to the Cliffside Park line. It runs from Anderson Avenue on the west to Briar Way and Buckingham Road on the east, and from Drury Lane and Euclid Road at the top down to Columbia Avenue, where the street railway right of way of the Hudson River Railroad and Ferry Company runs between the two carriageways of Columbia Avenue. The North Hudson Railway Company right of way runs down the middle of the sheet between the two halves of Washington Avenue. East of it the curving streets of a laid-out suburb (Dorincourt Road, Bridle Way, Dearborn Road, Cumbermede Road, Palisades Avenue, Briar Way) are lettered with the tract name of the Hudson River View Realty Company. Most lots are numbered but empty; the houses drawn are scattered frame and stucco dwellings, mostly two storey, with garages, concentrated along Anderson Avenue, Edgewood Lane and Washington Avenue. Buildings of note are an unfinished church on Bridle Way, a hose reel house of the volunteer fire company on Edgewood Lane, a fire department hose reel shed near Columbia Avenue, and a real estate office, restaurant, store and post office at the corner of Palisades Avenue and Columbia Avenue. Water pipes (6, 8 and 12 inch) are shown in most streets. The lower edge shows the outlines of sheets 52, 53 and 54, and the upper left corner part of sheet 61's block numbering; the adjoining sheets 52 to 54 are not part of this scan set.
notes: Washington Avenue is now Abbott Boulevard; it is drawn as two roads either side of the North Hudson Railway right of way.
Cumbermede Road is spelled Cumbermeade Road in OpenStreetMap.
Unfinished church on Bridle Way.
Columbia Avenue is drawn as two roadways with the Hudson River Railroad and Ferry Company street railway between them.

Fort Lee, southwest (Palisade section by the Cliffside Park line): Anderson Av east to Briar Way, Drury Lane to Columbia Av; Washington Av (now Abbott Boulevard), Edgewood Lane, Dorincourt Rd, Bluff Rd, Dearborn Rd, Cumbermede Rd, Bridle Way, Palisades Av, Euclid Rd, Buckingham Rd, Brook Lane. One part. Scale 100 ft.

sheet-56.description: Sheet 56, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the northwest edge of Fort Lee and a strip of Leonia beyond the boundary line. Main Street crosses the top of the sheet diagonally, meeting Central Avenue (now Fort Lee Road) at the upper left and Hoeflers Lane, Jones Road and Summit Avenue, which run off the top edge toward sheet 59 and 60. Bergen Boulevard, 80 feet wide, runs straight down the sheet; the Leonia boundary line follows its west side, so the blocks numbered 263 to 266 west of it, along Irving Street, a 20-foot lane, Beckwith and Lester Streets, are in Leonia. East of the boulevard the blocks between Bergen Boulevard, Maple Street and Main Street (blocks 40 to 42) are divided into narrow numbered lots with scattered frame dwellings of one to two and a half storeys, sheds, a saloon and a barber shop on Main Street, and a group of buildings named Woodside Villa. The large block 40 east of Maple Street is cut into long irregular lots with a few dwellings and a garage. At the upper right Jane and Catherine Streets meet John Street, with dwellings, a store, a flat and wagon sheds near Main Street. The lower half of the sheet is almost empty: block 267 is undeveloped, bounded by an unnamed street, John Street and North Avenue, and 5th Street and Main Avenue at the lower right are platted streets with nothing built. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches are shown in Main Street, Maple Street and the street between blocks 41 and 42. Adjoining sheets 57, 58, 59 and 60 are referenced in the margins.
notes: The Fort Lee and Leonia boundary line is drawn along the west side of Bergen Boulevard.
Central Avenue is now Fort Lee Road; Hoeflers Lane is now Hoefleys Lane.
The unnamed 20-foot lane west of Bergen Boulevard is modern Christie Lane.

Lester Street and Washington Terrace (probably the drawn Beckwith Street) did not agree with the other control (10 to 25 m) and were left out; modern Bergen Boulevard lies near the west edge of the drawn boulevard.
Main Avenue, 5th Street and the street marked 'No Name' were platted but undeveloped in 1911.

Fort Lee north edge and part of Leonia, 100 ft: Main St/Central Av at top, Bergen Blvd (Leonia line on its west side), Irving, Maple, Beckwith, Lester, Jane, Catherine, John Sts, North Av, 5th St, Main Av; blocks 263-267, mostly vacant. One part. Low-medium confidence; 2 hand-picked points.

sheet-57.description: Sheet 57, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, covers a largely vacant platted tract on the west side of Fort Lee, between Ann Street and Anderson Avenue and from the blocks north of Centre Street down to Main Avenue. North Avenue, 50 feet wide, crosses the middle of the sheet and Main Avenue runs below it; between them the numbered streets 5th, 4th, 3rd and 2nd Streets run north to south, with West Street and Ann Street entering from the north. Anderson Avenue forms the right edge, bending to the southeast near Main Avenue, where it is also labelled Tom Hunter Road, with a 12-inch water pipe along it. The blocks are numbered 268 to 274 and are mostly divided into lots with nothing built on them; block 274 below Main Avenue and blocks 270 and 271 are drawn as empty outlines. Development is limited to a few frame dwellings of two to two and a half storeys with sheds and stables: some on Ann Street in block 268, one dwelling drawn from plans near West Street, a row of dwellings in block 269 south of Centre Street, one dwelling in block 272, and a dwelling, small outbuildings, a wagon shed and a well in block 273 near Anderson Avenue. A narrow street at the upper left is marked 'Not Named', 33 feet wide. Streets are drawn 50 feet wide except Ann Street at 33 feet. Adjoining sheets 56, 58 and 61 are referenced in the margins.
notes: Centre Street is now Center Street.
The numbered streets have been renumbered: old 5th, 4th, 3rd and 2nd Streets correspond to modern 10th, 11th, 12th and 13th Streets at North Avenue.
Main Avenue does not survive under that name; no modern junction on it was used.
All control lies along Centre Street and North Avenue in the upper half; the lower half (Main Avenue, block 274) is placed by extrapolation.
Sheet dated in the lower right corner 'B.P. 2/4/11'.
Fort Lee west, 50 ft: Ann, West, Centre St, North Av, old 2nd-5th Sts (now 13th-10th), Main Av, Anderson Av; blocks 268-274 mostly vacant. One part. Control only along Centre St and North Av.

sheet-58.description: Sheet 58, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, shows the old grid of Fort Lee north of Anderson Avenue, in the blocks between John Street at the top and Anderson Avenue at the bottom, and from a short unnamed street and Centre Street on the west to Main Street, whose west frontage forms the right edge of the sheet. The north-south streets are Elizabeth, Catherine and Jane Streets; the cross streets are John, Ann and William Streets, all drawn 33 feet wide, with West Street entering from sheet 57 on the left. The blocks are divided into narrow numbered lots and built up only in part, with scattered one- to two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings, sheds, wagon sheds and a few stables. The densest frontage is along Main Street at the right edge, where there are stores, a saloon and a group of warehouses for groceries, gasoline and paints near Anderson Avenue. Bethany M.E. Church stands on Main Street at the corner of William Street. A frame dwelling with an attic stands alone in the large empty block 33 at the upper left, and a dwelling at the lower left is noted as fronting on Centre Street. A 12-inch water pipe runs along Anderson Avenue and a 6-inch pipe along Elizabeth Street. The upper part of the sheet beyond John Street is left blank and belongs to sheet 56; adjoining sheets 57, 60, 62 and 67 are referenced in the margins.
notes: Bethany M.E. Church on Main Street at William Street.
Centre Street is now Center Street.
John Street was left out of the fit: its two junctions sat 3.5 to 4.4 m off the other points, which suggests the modern street is slightly off its 1911 line.
An unnamed street ('No Name') runs along the left edge north of John Street.
Fort Lee centre north of Anderson Av: Main St, John, Ann, William Sts, Elizabeth, Catherine, Jane Sts, West St, Centre St. Bethany M.E. Church. One part. Scale 50 ft.

sheet-59.description: Sheet 59, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, covers the area north of Main Street on the Fort Lee and Leonia line, turned on the page so that north points to the upper left. Main Street, continuing west as Central Avenue, runs along the bottom edge, with Bergen Boulevard and Maple Street leaving it to the south. Jones Road crosses the sheet diagonally from the top to Main Street; Hoeflers Lane, 25 feet wide, runs from Main Street to the upper left, where another stretch of Hoeflers Lane turns northeast to Jones Road. Caspers Lane runs between Hoeflers Lane and Jones Road, and Summit Avenue leaves Jones Road to the east near the bottom right. The Leonia boundary line follows Hoeflers Lane and then the northwest edge of block 44, so block 43 and the land west of the lane lie in Leonia. Block 44 holds the R.C. Church of Madonna (stone spire, steam heat) and its rectory. Public School No. 2, of brick, stands on Jones Road in block 39, and a group of long greenhouses with sheds occupies block 38 east of Jones Road. The rest of the sheet is a loose scatter of frame dwellings of one to two and a half storeys, sheds, barns and wagon sheds on large lots, with stores, a saloon and dwellings fronting Main Street. A 6-inch water pipe runs in Hoeflers Lane and Jones Road and an 8-inch pipe in Main Street and Central Avenue. The upper right quarter of the sheet is blank. Adjoining sheets 56 and 60 are referenced in the margins.
notes: R.C. Church of Madonna and rectory in block 44; Public School No. 2 on Jones Road; greenhouses in block 38.
Hoeflers Lane is now Hoefleys Lane; the stretch running northeast to Jones Road is now Church Lane; Central Avenue is now Fort Lee Road.
Modern Caspar Lane does not follow the drawn Caspers Lane and was not used.
Church Lane / Hoefleys Lane, at the left edge, disagreed with the other control by about 10 m and was left out; the Leonia side of the sheet is placed by extrapolation.
The Fort Lee and Leonia boundary line is drawn along Hoeflers Lane.

Fort Lee and part of Leonia north of Main St, 50 ft: Jones Rd, Hoeflers Lane (upper stretch now Church Lane), Caspers Lane, Summit Av; R.C. Church of Madonna, Public School No 2, greenhouses. One part. Low confidence (5 points, 1 hand-picked).

sheet-60.description: Sheet 60, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the Linwood Park tract on the north side of Fort Lee, between Jones Road on the west and Linwood Avenue on the east, and from beyond West Street at the top down to Main Street at the bottom. The tract is laid out in long blocks of narrow numbered lots along Ellery Avenue, Edwin Avenue and Fletcher Avenue, crossed by West Street, Lee Street, Kelby Street and Lewis Street, with South Street between Fletcher and Linwood Avenues. Very little is built: scattered one- to three-storey frame dwellings, a few of brick, and sheds, most of them along Fletcher Avenue near Main Street and along South Street and Linwood Avenue. In the lower left, a separate block between Jones Road and a short bend of Summit Avenue holds a row of small lots facing Summit Avenue, with Fire Department Protection No. 3 (a hook and ladder truck with 200 feet of hose and an acoustic alarm) at the corner of Jones Road and Summit Avenue, and an artificial stone dwelling. Block 38, between Jones Road and the tract, is largely open ground with a few unlabelled buildings. On Main Street near Ann Street are a store and the Republican Club. The ends of John, Ann and William Streets are shown below Main Street at the bottom edge, and the sheet refers to the adjoining sheets 56, 58, 59 and 67. Water pipes are drawn in Main Street, Fletcher Avenue, Edwin Avenue and Linwood Avenue.
notes: Fire Department Protection No. 3 at Jones Road and Summit Avenue.
Republican Club on Main Street.

The middle of the sheet (Lee, Kelby and Lewis Streets) lies under the George Washington Bridge approach and New Jersey Turnpike; Lee Street no longer exists, and Kelby and Lewis Streets were left out of the fit (their junctions sat 5 to 9 m off). The placement rests on West Street, Main Street and Jones Road.
Summit Avenue was also left out (Jones Road junction 7.9 m off).
Fort Lee north of Main St: Ellery, Edwin, Fletcher, Lewis, Kelby, Lee, West, South, Linwood Avs, Summit Av, Jones Rd (Linwood Park tract). One part. Scale 100 ft.

sheet-61.description: Sheet 61, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, covers the southwest edge of Fort Lee between Anderson Avenue at the top and Eickhoft Street at the bottom, turned on the page so that north points to the upper right. Tom Hunter Road, 40 feet wide, runs down the middle of the sheet from Anderson Avenue across Centre Avenue (60 feet) toward the street railway; Whitman Street runs along the right edge to Eickhoft Street. At the upper left Anderson Avenue bends southwest past the end of Main Avenue, and North Avenue and Centre Street enter Anderson Avenue from the north along the top margin. The large block 288 west of Tom Hunter Road is entirely empty. East of the road, block 21 1/2 has a row of narrow lots fronting Anderson Avenue with frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half storeys and sheds, and a few more dwellings and a stable toward Whitman Street; its southern part is vacant. Block 20, between Centre Avenue and the street railway, holds Cella's Park Hotel, a large dance hall attached to it, and wagon sheds and a dwelling behind them. A street railway right of way crosses the lower part of the sheet diagonally, cutting off block 289, which fronts Eickhoft Street at the bottom edge. Water pipes of 12 inches in Anderson Avenue and 6 inches in Whitman Street are shown. Adjoining sheets 57 and 62 are referenced in the margins.
notes: Cella's Park Hotel and its dance hall stand in block 20 on Centre Avenue.
Whitman Street is now Whiteman Street; Eickhoft Street is now Gerome Avenue; Centre Avenue is now Center Avenue.
The street railway right of way appears to follow the line of the modern Abbott Boulevard footpath.
Eickhoft Street is cut by the bottom edge of the sheet; its junction with Whitman Street lies on the edge.
Fort Lee southwest, 50 ft: Anderson Av, Tom Hunter Rd, Centre Av, Whitman St, street railway right of way, Eickhoft St; Cella's Park Hotel and dance hall. One part.

sheet-62.description: Sheet 62, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, covers the centre of Fort Lee south of Anderson Avenue, between Whitman Street on the west and Main Street on the east, from Anderson Avenue at the top to Eickhoft Street at the bottom. Centre Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet and Hoym Street runs north-south through it; south of Centre Avenue Hoym Street is marked as not opened. A street railway right of way crosses the lower third diagonally, cutting the blocks between Centre Avenue and Eickhoft Street. The frontage along Anderson Avenue is lined with two- to two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings, with a painter's shop and a store near Main Street. The interior blocks are large and mostly open; along Main Street stand dwellings and villas, among them Clara Villa and Rosedale Villa, a boarding house and an office. At the corner of Main Street and Centre Avenue is the Fort Lee Hotel with a saloon, wagon shed and garage, and further south on Main Street another saloon. Near Whitman Street are a stone dwelling, a brick-veneered house with a cement block porch, and a row of two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings along Eickhoft Street. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches run in Main Street, Anderson Avenue, Centre Avenue, Whitman Street and Eickhoft Street. The upper edge shows the ends of Elizabeth, Catherine and Jane Streets from sheet 58, and the margins refer to sheets 61, 63, 64 and 67.
notes: Whitman Street is now Whiteman Street; Centre Avenue is Center Avenue; Eickhoft Street is now Gerome Avenue.
Hoym Street south of Centre Avenue is marked 'not opened' in 1911; it is open today.
Fort Lee Hotel (saloon) at Main Street and Centre Avenue; Clara Villa and Rosedale Villa on Main Street.
The two junctions on Eickhoft Street at Whitman Street and Main Street were hand-picked from the drawn block corners plus half the labelled widths.
Fort Lee centre: Anderson Av to Eickhoft St between Whitman St and Main St; Centre Av, Hoym St, street railway right of way; Fort Lee Hotel. One part. Scale 50 ft.

sheet-63.description: Sheet 63, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page, covers the centre of Fort Lee south of Main Street, between Eickhoft Street on the left edge and Palisades Avenue on the right, down to Whitman Street at the bottom. Main Street crosses the top of the sheet diagonally, with Lemoine Avenue leaving it northward at the upper left. Schlosser Street runs south from Main Street to Hoym Street, which crosses the left half of the sheet diagonally to Eickhoft Street; a ditch runs diagonally through block 13 between Main Street and Hoym Street. Pond Street leaves Palisades Avenue eastward on the right. The Main Street frontage is the busiest part: Schlosser's Fort Lee Club House with a saloon, stores, a bakery with its oven, wagon sheds and stables near the corner of Palisades Avenue. Along Schlosser Street and Palisades Avenue stand two- to two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings, with Kinsler's Bergen County Parcel Delivery on Palisades Avenue and a carpenter's shop of stone off Schlosser Street. The Cemmendinger furniture storage building stands on Eickhoft Street. In the lower part of the sheet the blocks are large and mostly empty, with Public School No. 1 (two and a half storeys of brick, furnace heat, electric light) near Whitman Street and a row of dwellings along Eickhoft Street. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches run in Main Street, Lemoine Avenue, Schlosser Street, Palisades Avenue, Eickhoft Street and Whitman Street.
notes: Public School No. 1 near Whitman Street.
Schlosser's Fort Lee Club House (saloon) on Main Street.
Eickhoft Street is now Gerome Avenue; Whitman Street is Whiteman Street; Palisades Avenue south of Main Street is Palisade Avenue.
Modern Lemoine Avenue south of Main Street is a newer road cutting diagonally through the 1911 blocks; it is not drawn here.
Placed on four points only, two of them hand-picked on Eickhoft Street; the Palisades Avenue side has no control. Low confidence.
Fort Lee centre: Main St south of Lemoine Av, Schlosser St, Hoym St, Eickhoft St, Whitman St, Palisades Av, Pond St; Public School No 1, Schlosser's Fort Lee Club House. One part. Scale 50 ft.

sheet-64-1.description: Sheet 64, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that Main Street runs down the left side, covers the centre of Fort Lee north and east of Main Street, from the Eickhoft Street corner at the top left to Hoyt Avenue along the bottom. Lemoine Avenue and Hudson Street run across the sheet from Main Street to the edge of sheet 67; Schlosser Street and Palisades Avenue are drawn only as short stubs on the far side of Main Street. A street railway right of way and a ditch cross the upper part of the sheet diagonally. The block between Main Street and the right of way holds Ferrando's Park Hotel with its saloon, restaurant and two-storey hall, a motion picture theatre, a cigar manufactory with stores and a livery stable. Main Street is lined with stores and dwellings, an insurance office, a five and ten cent store, a saloon, a wagon painting shed, a wheelwright and blacksmith shop, a cobbler and a building of patent stone. Lemoine Avenue and Hudson Street are lined with two- and two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings on long narrow lots, with a parochial school on Lemoine Avenue and carpenter shops behind. Between Hudson Street and Hoyt Avenue stands the Franchi Brothers furniture factory, with a cement block dwelling nearby. In the upper right the outline of the Abbott Piano Action Company works is drawn with a note referring to the detachment on the same sheet, which is boxed separately. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches run in Main Street, Lemoine Avenue, Hudson Street and Hoyt Avenue; the margins refer to sheets 62, 63, 66, 67 and 68.
notes: Hudson Street of 1911 meets Main Street where Park Avenue does today; the modern Hudson Street south of Central Avenue is a later street cut through the block between Lemoine Avenue and Hudson Street.
Hoyt Avenue of 1911 between Main Street and Cross Street no longer exists south of the George Washington Bridge plaza; it met Main Street opposite Parker Avenue, with a jog of about 14 m.
Eickhoft Street is lettered 'Eichoft St.' on this sheet; it is now Gerome Avenue.
Ferrando's Park Hotel, a motion picture theatre, a cigar manufactory, a parochial school and the Franchi Brothers furniture factory are drawn on this part.

The sheet is placed from one hand-picked junction, one detected junction and five block corners carried from sheets 63 and 66, all along Main Street; position away from Main Street (the Hoyt Avenue and Lemoine Avenue ends towards sheet 67) is extrapolated and low confidence.

Fort Lee centre east of Main St: Lemoine Av, Hudson St (now Park Av at Main), Hoyt Av (gone), Schlosser and Eickhoft stubs; Ferrando's Park Hotel, motion picture theatre, parochial school, Franchi Bros furniture factory. Part 1 main map (low confidence: only Main St survives as control, drawn about 6 percent long, rotation held by a derived point); part 2 boxed detachment of the Abbott Piano Action Co works, unplaced. Scale 50 ft.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: boxed detachment: Abbott Piano Action Co works (no street junction; needs step 6b: building corners carried from sheet-67-1 (works drawn at Lemoine Av)).

sheet-65-1.description: Sheet 65, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page, covers the southeastern corner of Fort Lee along the Edgewater line, from Palisades Avenue at the top to River Road and Main Street at the bottom, and from the top of the Palisades bluff on the left to Pond Street and East Palisades Avenue on the right. Parker Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet. North of Parker Avenue are scattered dwellings, a pigeon house, a glazing shop, the Episcopal church and a public park laid out with crossing paths around a monument stone at Pond Street. South of Parker Avenue the land is mostly open: the Fort Lee and Edgewater boundary line follows the top of the high bluff across the sheet and then runs down Massa's Lane, also lettered Delafolie Place. Gerth's Belvedere Hotel with its restaurant, kitchen and a second hotel building stands near East Palisades Avenue, with a wagon shed at its corner with Federspiel Street. River Road comes up the bluff from the lower left and joins Main Street, with Annett Avenue below it in Edgewater. A boxed detachment at the left, drawn at its own orientation, shows a large stone residence placed only by distances (700 feet to Palisades Avenue, 750 feet to Whitman Street); it is a separate part. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches run in Palisades Avenue, Parker Avenue and River Road.
notes: Pond Street is now Monument Place; East Palisades Avenue is now Old Palisade Road; Massa's Lane is now Massa Lane (its northern part has been realigned).
The public park at Pond Street with the monument stone is today's Monument Park.
Gerth's Belvedere Hotel and the Episcopal church are drawn on this part.
The Fort Lee and Edgewater boundary line follows the top of the bluff and Massa's Lane.
Placed from four detected junctions and one hand-picked junction (Massa Lane / River Road); the western half of the part, on the bluff, has no control of its own.

Fort Lee southeast at the Edgewater line: Palisades Av, Parker Av, Pond St (Monument Place), E. Palisades Av (Old Palisade Road), Massa's Lane / Delafolie Pl, River Rd, Annett Av, Main St; Episcopal church, public park, Gerth's Belvedere Hotel. Part 1 main map; part 2 boxed stone residence placed only by distances, unplaced. Scale 50 ft.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: boxed detachment: large stone residence (no street junction; placed on the sheet only by distances (700 ft to Palisades Av, 750 ft to Whitman St)).

sheet-66.description: Sheet 66, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page, covers the east centre of Fort Lee south of Main Street, between Palisades Avenue at the top and Main Street, which bends around the right side and the bottom of the sheet. Pond Street, English Street and Cedar Street run down the sheet from Palisades Avenue; Parker Avenue, Federspiel Street and Kaufer's Lane run across it, and East Palisades Avenue curves down the left side to Main Street. The block at Palisades Avenue and Main Street holds the First National Bank, a photographer, a blacksmith shop and stores, and the house of Fire Department Protection Company No. 1 with a belfry on its roof. The Main Street frontage between Parker Avenue and Kaufer's Lane is lined with stores and dwellings, two plumbers, a paint and oils store, a hay and feed store, a blacksmith and A. Vogel's machine shop. The interior blocks are residential, with two- and two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings, a patent stone building on Federspiel Street and a cement block dwelling near the bottom, where a saloon stands at the corner of East Palisades Avenue and Main Street. Cedar Street and Kaufer's Lane are only 20 feet wide. The right margin shows Hoyt Avenue, Siegman Street and Bigler Street on the far side of Main Street, belonging to sheets 64 and 68, and Hudson Terrace at the lower right. Water pipes of 6 inches run in most streets.
notes: Pond Street is now Monument Place; East Palisades Avenue is now Old Palisade Road; Kaufer's Lane is now Kaufers Lane.
In 1911 Federspiel Street ended at Cedar Street; today it continues to Main Street. Cedar Street and Kaufer's Lane are drawn 20 feet wide.
First National Bank and the house of Fire Department Protection Company No. 1 at Palisades Avenue and Main Street.

The junction of Cedar Street and Kaufer's Lane was hand-picked (the 20 ft streets are too narrow for the detector); the junction of East Palisades Avenue and Main Street at the bottom was left out (5 m off).
Fort Lee east centre south of Main St: Parker Av, English, Cedar, Federspiel Sts, Kaufer's Lane, Pond St, E. Palisades Av; First National Bank, Fire Dept. Protection Co. No. 1. One part. Scale 50 ft.

sheet-67-1.description: Sheet 67, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page, covers the north and east of Fort Lee above Main Street, from Linwood Avenue along the left edge to Hoyt Avenue at the right, with Main Street along the bottom. Centre Avenue runs diagonally up the left half of the sheet, joined by Guntzer Street near Main Street; a street railway right of way with a ditch runs beside it. Further right Lemoine Avenue, Hudson Street and Hoyt Avenue run parallel up the sheet, crossed near the top right by Cross Street. The lower left is taken by the Collegiate Institute of the Holy Angels, a girls' school, with its school and convent, chapel, kitchen and laundry, priest's house and heating plant; a stone dwelling and a garage stand on the block between Guntzer Street and Main Street. Most of the sheet is laid out in long narrow lots, many still vacant, with scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings along Centre Avenue, Lemoine Avenue and Hudson Street, a greenhouse, a piano repairing factory near Lemoine Avenue and the outline of the Abbott Piano Action Company works, which is drawn in detail on sheet 64. The ground south of Lemoine Avenue near the right of way is left blank for sheet 64, and the lower right corner carries a boxed inset drawn at its own orientation, which is a separate part. West Street, Kelby Street and Lewis Street are lettered as stubs at the left edge, Anderson Avenue below Main Street. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches run in Linwood Avenue, Centre Avenue, Lemoine Avenue, Hudson Street and Main Street.
notes: Centre Avenue is now Center Avenue.

The George Washington Bridge approach, Bridge Plaza and the New Jersey Turnpike now cross the middle of this sheet; Hoyt Avenue and Cross Street have been largely erased or realigned (modern Hoyt Avenue lies about 30 m west of the drawn one at the top of the sheet).
Collegiate Institute of the Holy Angels (for girls) with school, convent and chapel at Linwood Avenue and Main Street.

Placed from four detected junctions along Main Street and a hand-picked junction of Linwood Avenue and West Street at the upper left; the upper right of the sheet (Hudson Street and Hoyt Avenue) has no control of its own, but drawn Lemoine Avenue lies within about 6 m of the modern street at the top of the sheet.

Fort Lee north and east of Main St: Linwood, Centre, Lemoine Avs, Hudson St, Hoyt Av, Guntzer and Cross Sts; Collegiate Institute of the Holy Angels. Part 1 main map; part 2 boxed inset (Central Av, Hudson Ter, Sylvan, Stanley, Cross) drawn at about 105 ft to the inch. Scale 100 ft.

sheet-67-2.description: The boxed inset in the lower right corner of sheet 67 has its own north arrow and is turned differently from the rest of the sheet. It shows the district east of Hoyt Avenue between Sylvan Street at the top and Cross Street at the bottom: Hoyt Avenue on the left, Central Avenue down the middle and Hudson Terrace on the right, crossed by Sylvan Street and by Stanley Street, a name marked as arbitrary. The blocks between Central Avenue and Hudson Terrace north of Stanley Street hold one- and two-storey frame dwellings and a saloon; the large block south of Stanley Street is almost empty apart from a pair of attached two-storey dwellings facing Central Avenue and a small house near Cross Street. The block between Hoyt Avenue and Central Avenue is divided into narrow vacant lots. East of Hudson Terrace are a restaurant and a storehouse for masons' material, noted as 150 feet east of Hudson Terrace. Central Avenue continues south of Cross Street onto sheet 68. Water pipes of 6 inches run in Central Avenue, Sylvan Street and Cross Street. The scale of the inset is not stated; the fit gives about 105 feet to an inch, slightly smaller than the 100 feet of the main sheet.
notes: Central Avenue of 1911 north of its bend is now Central Road; Stanley Street (arbitrary) is now Merkle Street; Sylvan Street keeps its name.
Cross Street has no surviving equivalent in OpenStreetMap; the George Washington Bridge plaza cuts across the south half of this inset.

Placed from four detected junctions (Central Road and Hudson Terrace at Sylvan Street and Merkle Street) that lie close together in the upper third; the Cross Street end is extrapolated and low confidence.

Fort Lee north and east of Main St: Linwood, Centre, Lemoine Avs, Hudson St, Hoyt Av, Guntzer and Cross Sts; Collegiate Institute of the Holy Angels. Part 1 main map; part 2 boxed inset (Central Av, Hudson Ter, Sylvan, Stanley, Cross) drawn at about 105 ft to the inch. Scale 100 ft.

sheet-68.description: Sheet 68, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, covers the eastern edge of Fort Lee north of Main Street, between Hoyt Avenue on the left and Hudson Terrace on the right, from Cross Street at the top to Main Street at the bottom. Central Avenue runs down from Cross Street and turns east to end at Bigler Street, which runs from Central Avenue down to Main Street; Siegman Street is a short stub off Main Street. Hudson Terrace runs diagonally down the right side to meet Main Street at the lower right, beyond which the ground is left blank. The Hoyt Avenue frontage and the blocks along Central Avenue are divided into long narrow lots with scattered two- and two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings, a power shed and a few outbuildings. The Main Street frontage is commercial: a drug store with the post office at the corner of Hoyt Avenue, stores and dwellings, a printing shop with an electric motor, an auto house and long shed, a saloon and hotel at Bigler Street, a wagon shed, a blacksmith and another saloon near Hudson Terrace. Kaufer's Lane is shown opposite Bigler Street on the south side of Main Street. Water pipes of 6 inches run in Hoyt Avenue, Central Avenue, Cross Street and Main Street; the margins refer to sheets 64, 66 and 67.
notes: The north-south arm of Central Avenue is now Central Road; its east-west arm is part of today's Central Avenue, which now continues past Bigler Street to Hudson Terrace.
Siegman Street and Cross Street do not survive under those names; Hoyt Avenue north of Main Street has been erased by the George Washington Bridge plaza.
Drug store and post office at Hoyt Avenue and Main Street.

Placed from one detected junction (Central Avenue and Central Road), two hand-picked junctions on Bigler Street and two block corners at Hoyt Avenue and Main Street carried from sheet 66; low confidence (residuals about 4 m, fitted scale about 3 percent off).

Fort Lee east, north of Main St: Hoyt Av, Central Av (now Central Road and Central Avenue), Bigler St, Siegman St, Cross St, Hudson Terrace. One part, low confidence (5 points, top extrapolated). Scale 50 ft.
